evidence.measurement_note: measured with in-process _reuse_candidate against the REAL graph 4790bbb1...897b; scratch pin copies only; SHORT pins already warned at every length before the change, the defect was the silent over-long case
evidence.rule_short: A pin is reported as reduced strength whenever it supplies fewer hex characters than the full 64-hex digest, at every such length (63 hex as loudly as 12) - there is no length threshold.
evidence.overlong_justification: A sha256 is exactly 64 hex, so a longer value is not an abbreviation of a digest but a corrupted or mis-edited one, and the old comparison honoured only its first 64 characters (65- and 100-hex pins matched with no notice and an unvalidated tail). It is refused exactly like a malformed/unreadable/empty pin - present-and-unusable, not a fresh setup. (b) validate-the-tail was rejected because it moves the comparison U8.11 fixed to the full digest; (c) accept-and-warn was rejected because a pin that 'matches' on a 64-char prefix while carrying corrupt trailing characters is the blessing this control exists to prevent.
evidence.overlong_what_caller_can_still_get_wrong: A 65+-hex pin now causes a refusing run to BUILD a fresh graph on a real (non-dry) run rather than silently reuse - the fail-closed direction, but a behaviour change an operator will see as a rebuild.

evidence.residual: No: after this change every pin that MATCHES emits a notice unless it is exactly the full 64 hex - 0/empty and 1-11 hex are refused (empty pin state / _same_digest's width>=12 floor), 12-63 warn PIN ABBREVIATED + REDUCED STRENGTH, exactly 64 is the only silent match and is full strength, >64 is refused PIN OVERLONG. What a caller can still get wrong is not length but presentation and provenance: (1) the printed graph line shows only 12 hex via _digest12 (display-only), so an operator cannot eyeball the tail - the full value is in counts['sha256']; (2) the committed config/graph_pin.toml comment still says 'a >=12-hex prefix is accepted for readability' and does not say >64 is now refused - a documentation residual, and that file is outside this unit's write paths (its commit is a checkpoint action); (3) a 64-hex pin that is correct for a graph the operator did not intend is still 'match' (the pin attests bytes, not semantics) and (4) the case-insensitive, whitespace-stripped comparison is intentional and loses no strength.
